what: first end-to-end run of MiniMaxH3VSAAttention on kijai's FastVideo VSA-distilled H3 checkpoint, against a dense control on the same checkpoint
answers: a MECHANICAL question only: does VSA run, is its gate consumed, is it deterministic. NOT whether the output is good.

stack.core: comfyanonymous/ComfyUI#15958 head 10febb01, a DRAFT, applied to this box's working tree

engaged: log line '[h3-vsa] VSA on 50 blocks, keep 10.0% of key blocks, 4x4x4 cubes, pooled_tail=False', and no fallback warning
verdict: VSA differs from its dense control and reproduces itself at the same seed, so the gate is consumed and the path is deterministic.
timing_caveat: NOT MEASURED, in either direction. One run per arm, 1.5 s apart. That cannot separate a 6% difference from run-to-run excursion, so this is neither evidence of a speedup nor evidence of its absence -- an earlier wording said 'no speedup', which is a claim this sample cannot support either way. The cold number carries the model load and is comparable to neither warm one; the two warm numbers share a cached text encode, which is what makes them comparable to each other at all.
not_established: any quality claim. A rendered pair cannot A/B a numerical change, and this pair additionally changes the attention regime outright.
that keep_percent 10.0 is right. It is the distillation's published sparsity, unmeasured here.
anything at the lengths this repo normally renders. 22,121 rows is far below the 31k-128k of the shipped graphs, and sparse attention's win grows with length.

container_hash_trap.why_file_hashes_lie: two mp4 container tags. format.tags.comment carries the whole API prompt under VHS save_metadata, so any two ARMS differ by construction; format.tags.creation_time is a wall clock, so any two RUNS differ, including two runs of one arm. Only the second explains two runs of one graph.
container_hash_trap.not_the_cause: the muxer and the codec. Checked, not assumed: remuxing one file twice and re-encoding it twice at the same settings each give identical bytes.
container_hash_trap.one_way_implication_survives: identical container still implies identical frames, so nothing concluded from a MATCHING hash is withdrawn.
container_hash_trap.shared_namespace: bench/smoke_h3.py hard-codes one _smoketest prefix, so every session on this box shares an output counter and consecutive files may belong to different sessions. Arm identity lives ONLY in the embedded comment tag. Verified for this record: 00007/00009 wire MiniMaxH3VSAAttention, 00008 does not, all three are the VSA checkpoint at seed 730451892; the adjacent 00006 is another session's PDD arm on fl2va at 39 frames.

shape_is_least_favourable_measured.so: 22,121 rows is below every shipped graph sampled, by 3x against the cheapest and 5x against the common ones. Sparse attention's advantage grows with sequence length, so this is close to the least favourable shape available -- a MEASURED statement now, not a hedge.
